event: 2025 ILCA 6 Women's & ILCA 7 Men's World Championships
procedural_matters: After receiving a report from the race committee, the international jury decided to call a hearing to consider whether the driver of MAS support vessel has broken a rule, under RRS 62.1.
Hugh Leicester (Principal Race Officer) was appointed by the international jury to present the allegations, under RRS 62.2.
Ferdinand Ziegelmayer (Boat Supplier) gave evidence as a witness for the Principal Race Officer.
MAS 209882, MAS 209883, MAS 214989, and the driver of the MAS support vessel did not come to the hearing. The hearing proceeded in accordance with RRS 63.1(b).
facts: On race day 5, course B, the race committee singnalled flag AP over A and flag T on water after race 2.
MAS 209882, MAS 209883, and MAS 214989 were towed by MAS ILCA 7 support vessel from the course returning to the harbour.
The race committee observed the towing speed of MAS 209882, MAS 209883 and MAS 214989 between 7.9 and 13 knots according to the trackers.
Sailing instructions 22.2 require that the towing speed of boats shall not exceed 6 knots.
conclusions: MAS 209882, MAS 209883, MAS 214989, and the driver of MAS ILCA 7 support vessel failed to comply with the speed limit as required by the sailing instructions and broke SI 22.2. Rules: RRS 62.1, RRS 62.2, RRS 62.4, RRS 63.1(b), SI 22.2
decision: The driver of the MAS ILCA 7 support vessel is penalised as follows: the driver of the MAS ILCA 7 and the support vessel of the MAS ILCA 7 are excluded from going afloat until all three fleets of the ILCA 7 class have started race 3.
MAS 209882, MAS 209883, and MAS 214989 are warned under RRS 62.4 that a penalty may be imposed if the driver of the MAS ILCA 7 support vessel commits a further breach of any rule.
